gap: No result ChatGPT got states what a shared-15 W USB strip delivers per port when several phones charge at once. ChargerLab measured 3.06 W, 4.67 W and 6.04 W across three ports of a Baseus PowerCombo 30 W strip, against about 25–29 W from one port alone.
standout_why: I could not read the one cited rival, Tom's Guide (tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-surge-protector). WebFetch returned only the title on three tries (US URL, /uk/ URL, and the /best-surge-protectors variant), and the archive was blocked, so I don't know whether it publishes USB measurements. Rank 2, rottenwifi.com, already says the Anker 351 'shares the available USB power', quotes the 15 W total from the Amazon listing, and says USB-C reaches 20 W only when the USB-A ports are idle. Rank 9, geekchamp.com, gives shared-budget warnings for other picks and says it has no USB measurements of its own. Rank 12, laptopbee.com, gives figures with no method (19 W into an iPhone 15 from an 'Anker PowerExtend 12-outlet'), names no meter and no tester, and does not cover the Anker 351, the Nano 67 W, TESSAN or onn. So the rivals already state the shared-budget caveat. What none of them has is a named lab's measured per-port split under load, and the only one I found is for a product that is not a candidate: a 220–240 V Baseus strip, not sold in the US.
decides: This supports the pick only indirectly. A shared 15 W USB budget gave about 3–6 W per phone in ChargerLab's three-phone test. That backs Dealectric's 'USB-C max' column, which says the Anker 351 gives 20 W only with the USB-A ports idle and 15 W shared otherwise. It also supports steering anyone who charges two or more devices at once toward the 67 W or 140 W Anker stations or the TESSAN 65 W hub. I found no named measurement of any actual candidate's output, so this cannot change the order of picks.

findings.label: Per-port USB output, three phones charging at once (shared budget)
